hints.content:
###Graphing the first point

To graph a line, we need to find two points that are on it. Then we can drag the movable points to those points.

We already have one point, $(-2,-3)$, and we can use the slope of the line to find another point.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The point negative two, negative three is plotted and labeled.

hints.content:
###Use the slope to graph another point

We want the slope to be $\dfrac87$. Let's look at this slope as a fraction to help us graph the line:

$\text{slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\maroonD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\maroonD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{8}}{\maroonD{7}}$

Starting at $(-2,-3)$, let's go $\purpleD{8\text{ units up}}$ and $\maroonD{7\text{ units to the right}}$ to plot another point on the line:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points negative two, negative three and five, five are plotted and labeled. There is a vertical dotted segment from negative two, negative three to negative two, five that is labeled eight. There is a horizontal dotted segment from negative two, five to five, five that is labeled seven.

question.content:
**Graph a line that contains the point $(-2,-3)$ and has a slope of $\dfrac87$.**
